title: Session-interference matrix harness for prefix-cache & queueing regression detection
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Objective: Build a reproducible harness that exercises continuous batching + queueing interactions across mixed tenant/session profiles and KV/prefix cache states to detect p95 latency regressions and throughput (tokens/sec) degradations when runtime or kernel changes are introduced.

Background: Prior work focused on single-profile probes and synthetic microbursts. Production traffic mixes long, stateful chat sessions (high KV affinity) with short stateless requests and sporadic bursts from ingestion pipelines. These mixes produce non-linear batching and queueing effects that can hide regressions (e.g., small kernel changes increasing p95 under intermittent cache churn). We need a benchmark that: (1) reproduces multi-profile interference, (2) manipulates prefix/KV cache warm/cold cycles, (3) varies batching-window heuristics and queueing discipline, and (4) applies automated regression detection.

Scope and deliverables:
- Harness that composes multiple arrival profiles (session-long, short-inference, microburst) with adjustable ratios and correlation parameters.
- Support for toggling KV/prefix cache behavior: fully cold, partially warm (per-tenant hot prefixes), and frequent eviction patterns.
- Parameters exposed: arrival distributions, target TPS, tokens-per-request distribution, model variant, batch-window ms, max-batch-size, queue-discipline (FIFO/prioritized), and simulated network latency.
- Metrics collected: tokens/sec, request/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, batch sizes distribution, queue length over time, KV hit-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and memory pressure.
- Regression detector that uses robust statistical methods: baseline-window comparisons (rolling 1h baseline), EWMA on p95, and non-parametric tests (Mann-Whitney U) for significance. Alerts should include effect sizes and confidence intervals.
- Dashboards and automated reports exported to the Console (or a temporary Grafana) and stored artifacts (CSV/Parquet) for offline analysis.
- Integration tests and a CI job that runs the harness in synthetic mode on small hardware for sanity checks, plus an overnight stress run on dedicated test cluster for signal-quality.

Test matrix (initial):
- Profiles: 60% chat sessions (long-tail tokens), 30% short requests (<=64 tokens), 10% ingest bursts (high tokens, low concurrency).
- Cache states: 100% warm / 50% hot prefixes / 0% warm (cold start) / periodic evictions at configurable rate.
- Batch-window: 0ms (no batching) / 10ms / 50ms / adaptive (current runtime heuristic).
- Queue discipline: FIFO / priority-by-latency-sensitivity / backpressure-based admission.
- Model variants: small fp16, quantized-int8, and a mid-size model to surface differences in batching efficacy.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can reproducibly create >30 minutes of stable mixed traffic with telemetry granularity <=1s.
- Regression detector correctly flags injected regressions: we will introduce controlled slowdowns (5–20% on token throughput or +10–50ms on p95) and verify detection within 30 minutes with <5% false positives in baseline runs.
- Dashboards show clear annotations for test phases and cache state transitions.
- CI job exists and runs in under 2 hours in synthetic mode; full nightly run is scheduled separately.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Fidelity vs. cost: Full-fidelity runs on GPU clusters are expensive; we will use a two-tier approach (fast synthetic mode for quick feedback + full runs for release gating).
- Statistical noise: Mixed workloads increase variance; use longer baselines and robust statistics to avoid false positives.
- Conservatism in thresholds may hide subtle regressions; include manual review paths for small effect sizes.

Implementation notes:
- Reuse the arrival-synthesis library from ENG-18340 where possible but extend it to retain session affinity and KV prefix correlation.
- Telemetry instrumentation should emit structured traces for request lifecycle (enqueue, batch-assemble, GPU execution, KV access) with request IDs to join metrics.
- Regression detector implemented as a small service (Python) that reads metrics streams, computes EWMA and non-parametric tests, and writes findings to the Console alerts API.
- Provide a CLI wrapper to regenerate test scenarios and a recipe file (YAML) for reproducibility.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Session+Interference+Matrix+Harness
- Arrival-synthesis RFC (notes): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sess-intro
- Prototype PR (load generator): https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-runner/pull/412
